Generics

Generic functions#

Type parameters go in angle brackets after the name.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
fn identitas<T>(T datum) → T {
    return datum
}

main {
    print identitas("Marcus")
    print identitas(42)
}

The same function serves both calls. T is fixed per call site, not erased to a dynamic value.

Generic with a union return#

Type parameters compose with unions, which is how "maybe nothing" is expressed generically.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
fn primum<T>(list<T> res) → T ∪ none {
    if res.length() ≡ 0 then return null
    return res[0]
}

main {
    print primum([1, 2, 3])
}

Generic containers#

The built-in collections are generic already.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
main {
    let list<string> nomina ← ["Marcus", "Julia"]
    let map<string, int> aetates ← { "Marcus": 30 }
    print nomina, aetates
}

Classes#

class (en class) declares a class with type-first fields. Each field names its mode: let is fixed after construction and mut is writable. A field with neither word is PARSE010 field_modifier_missing, and a ref field is PARSE010 ref_field_refused.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
class Persona {
    let string nomen
    let int aetas
}

fn description(Persona p) → string {
    return p.nomen
}

main {
    let _ p ← Persona { nomen = "Marcus", aetas = 30 }
    print description(p)
}

Functions on a class#

A class can carry functions alongside its fields.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
class Punctum {
    let int x
    let int y

    fn sum() → int {
        return self.x + self.y
    }
}

main {
    let _ p ← Punctum { x = 1, y = 2 }
    print p.summa()
}

self — "I" — is the receiver, what other languages spell this or self.
